summary: Comprehensive test of Houzz Proposal Import + Purchase Orders. 18/18 backend pytest tests PASSED. Full frontend flow verified: PO dashboard, Houzz importer modal (all data-testids present), PO detail modal with manufacturer_link column (ZERO retailer leaks), payment recording (deposit -> deposit_paid status transition confirmed live), per-project PO tab rendered between FF&E and Whole Home Finishes and correctly hides Project column when scoped. Manufacturer resolver correctly swaps Wayfair->uttermost.com, Amazon->fourhands.com, keeps direct visualcomfort.com, and returns null for unknown-brand+retailer combos with a warning.

ui_bugs.issue: Pasting a non-Houzz URL (e.g., https://example.com) and clicking Start produced NO visible validation error message. The modal appeared to accept it silently. If validation is meant to trigger, it is silent — user won't know why nothing happens.

action_items: OPTIONAL: Add a visible validation error in HouzzProposalImporter when the URL is not a pro.houzz.com/manage/d/estimates/* URL. Currently the Start click is a silent no-op.

OPTIONAL: /app/memory/test_credentials.md lists project id 72d4051a-...-fb0fec94f250 but the real project id in DB is f694f389-29ff-4190-9bd8-a64f2000b54d — update this doc so future test agents don't hit 404s.
critical_code_review_comments: manufacturer_resolver.py — solid, forbidden list is comprehensive (33 retailers). Suggest adding 'joybird.com', 'article.com', 'burke-decor.com' if they surface later.
purchase_orders.py._apply_payment_status uses float equality tolerance of 0.005 — good. Watch for very large POs where cumulative rounding could cross that threshold, but not a bug today.
houzz_import.commit_session uses items[0]['brand'] as vendor for a PO — if line items have mixed brands, vendor is misleading. Consider concatenating or letting user choose vendor before commit.
purchase_orders.import_from_pdf: brand extracted by first two capitalized tokens can miscategorize (e.g. 'Ashford Dining' -> brand 'Ashford Dining'). Improvement, not a blocker.
Both PDF import handlers embed reportlab-generated PDFs successfully via PyPDF2. Good fallback to pdfplumber.
